nodes.label: Privacy Policy / Data Safety Drift
nodes.rationale: store/PRIVACY_POLICY.md (effective 2026-05-17) states 'No analytics or usage telemetry' and 'No crash reports or diagnostics', and store/STORE_LISTING.md's Data Safety Form Answers likewise claim only the AdMob Advertising ID is collected. website/public/privacy.html (last updated 2026-08-21) instead discloses Firebase Crashlytics (crash stack traces + device info), Google Analytics for Firebase (usage events), and Firebase Performance Monitoring (startup/rendering/network timings) as active third-party services. The two policy versions directly contradict each other on real SDK behaviour, which is exactly the class of issue mvp-plan.html's blocking gate B4 ('Data Safety form matches real SDK behaviour') flags as unresolved.

nodes.label: "Fleet Health Score" marketing claim
nodes.rationale: Markets 'See your Fleet Health Score the moment you open the app' as a headline feature, while PLAN.md records the health score as deleted (four competing formulas, one scored UNKNOWN as 100/100) on 2026-08-16 — a truthful-store-copy risk.

nodes.label: AutoMinder Pro "7-day free trial" claim
nodes.rationale: Lists 'Cloud backup & sync' and a '7-day free trial' for AutoMinder Pro, which implies a subscription trial mechanic, conflicting with PRD.md's and CLAUDE.md's one-time $4.99 purchase (never subscription) policy and with cloud sync being deferred indefinitely.

nodes.label: Performance gates (S1-S3, Baseline Profile unwired)
nodes.rationale: Baseline Profile plugin applied with no producer module; no macrobenchmark/jank measurement, so every performance claim across the docs is unmeasured.

nodes.label: Stability & performance checklist (Baseline Profile gap)
nodes.rationale: Baseline Profile plugin applied but no producer module exists (settings.gradle.kts includes only :app) — no profile is actually generated; fine to ship 1.0 without it but queued for 1.1.

nodes.label: Monetization strategy ($4.99 one-time, never subscription)
nodes.rationale: Free + one-time-purchase model chosen because research shows users viscerally reject subscriptions for utility apps (Drivvo's 4x price hike cited); conflicts with the Play listing copy's '7-day free trial' framing, which implies a subscription.

nodes.label: Speed & architecture recommendations (Android-specific)
nodes.rationale: Baseline Profiles + startup profile already in the TOML but not actually wired — the single biggest win available on mid-range phones; recommends macrobenchmark for cold start target < 800ms.

nodes.label: AdMob ID Production Safety Gate Pattern
nodes.norm_label: admob id production safety gate pattern
nodes.rationale: Debug builds hardcode Google's official test IDs (the sanctioned pattern); release IDs come from RELEASE_ADMOB_ID/ADMOB_APP_ID via env or local.properties, falling back to the literal string 'PLACEHOLDER' (never a test ID, never empty). A Production Safety Gate in build.gradle.kts fails any assembleRelease/bundleRelease task with a GradleException if the resolved release ID is null, blank, or 'PLACEHOLDER' -- this gate must never be weakened.

nodes.label: Play Billing 7.1.1 to 9.1.0 Migration
nodes.rationale: Google Play rejects Billing Library 7 for new apps/updates after 2026-08-31 (extension 2026-11-01 via Console form). AutoMinder is unpublished, so this deadline binds the initial submission. Migration to 9.x must occur alone on migration/play-billing-9, never bundled with UI/Ads/Room/navigation/release-workflow changes, so a failed migration cannot be entangled with unrelated regressions.

nodes.label: Demo Data Credibility Issue
nodes.rationale: Live, rendered demo data shows 'Overdue by 173,000 km' -- a real, not hypothetical, implausible value that undermines every QA screenshot taken while it persists. Tracked as HANDOFF.md Slice 8 nit #7 and as mvp-plan.html's blocking gate B8; both argue it should move earlier rather than stay a final-polish item, since store screenshots depend on it.

nodes.label: Four Bottom Navigation Tabs (Home/Vehicles/Records/Settings)
nodes.rationale: PRD.md documents 3 tabs (Dashboard/Vehicles/Settings) with ServiceHistory nested inside VehicleDetail, but the shipped app has 4 top-level tabs with Records promoted to its own destination. Code and CLAUDE.md are authoritative; Records must never be renamed or demoted back into VehicleDetail.

nodes.label: Fuel Intelligence Algorithm Phases (v1.1+)
nodes.rationale: A four-phase confidence model (seed from vehicle-DB prior at 0 fill-ups, Bayesian updating at 1-4, EMA alpha=0.25 at 5-9, seasonal-adjusted adaptive alpha at 10+, with confidence_low_km triggering a reminder under 50km) is reserved for v1.1+. PRD.md lists Fuel Intelligence as v1.0 scope (P9 YES), but CLAUDE.md overrides and defers it; it must not be implemented or wired up while v1.0 is feature-frozen.

nodes.label: Health Score Fabrication / Banned Language
nodes.rationale: Three unreconciled 0-100 health-score formulas exist simultaneously (FleetHealthScore.calculateHealthScore, DashboardScreen's inline fleetScore, VehicleDetailScreen's computeHealthScore); Dashboard's fleetScore has no guard and would show 100 for a brand-new fleet with zero data, violating the truthful-absence rule. Five vehicle_health_* strings and cd_health_score use the literally banned 'Vehicle Health'/'Health score' phrases, which are read aloud to every TalkBack user. Fix: pass score=null at both HealthCockpitCard call sites and delete FleetHealthScore.kt once confirmed dead.

nodes.label: Locale Claims Mismatch (Gate B5)
nodes.rationale: localeFilters declares es and pt-rBR, but only the English values/ resource set actually exists -- advertising Spanish and Portuguese support while shipping English-only is judged a false store claim, not polish. The honest MVP fix is to drop the locale filters and launch English-only, deferring real translation to v1.1.

nodes.label: Midnight Cobalt Design System
nodes.rationale: The accent colour IS the healthy state: cobalt sits at hue 214°, 176° from the caution band (the maximum possible separation), so only amber (due-soon) and red (overdue) ever interrupt a screen. Dark is the primary theme because the app is used in driveways and garages after dark, but light is first-class parity, not an afterthought. Pure black (#000000) is banned because it maximises OLED halation and smears on scroll; #0F1316 stays dark while leaving elevation headroom.

nodes.label: Mobbin Competitive Research Pass 2
nodes.rationale: 10 live search_screens queries (not the ~30 budgeted) against Mercedes-Benz, My BMW, Tesla, and category apps; a natural-language 'car maintenance dashboard' query failed entirely (returned a BNPL app, a habit tracker, a breathing app) because Mobbin has no maintenance-app category. BMW's 'NEXT SERVICES' flat list -- dual-basis date-or-distance phrasing, urgency carried by colour+icon only, no chips or filled badges -- was found to be the single most relevant screen and corroborates (rather than originates) the sentence-first, no-score-ring Home direction already decided from repository evidence in Pass 1.

nodes.label: AutoMinder MVP Plan Thesis
nodes.rationale: AutoMinder does not win on logging -- the market is full of maintenance loggers -- it wins on one promise: the reminder arrives on time, and everything it says is true. That leaves exactly three things worth being best at: the reminder fires correctly, nothing shown is invented, and logging costs almost nothing. Charts, OCR, analytics, and silhouettes are decoration on top of those three and must not ship until all three are proven.

nodes.label: No-Photo Law
nodes.rationale: Vehicle.photoUri is nullable and Add Vehicle folds the photo behind progressive disclosure, so no-photo is the realistic majority case, not an edge case. The premium baseline must be carried by make/model, year, mileage, status, typography and cobalt hierarchy alone. Manufacturer press imagery, stock photography, or AI-generated vehicles must never substitute for a missing photo -- a missing photo is a fact about this user's garage, not a hole to fill with a prettier lie. It is a required proof state, proven first, not last.

nodes.label: Precision Rail Status Indicator
nodes.rationale: PremiumStatusStyle.railColor() returns the leading accent rule for OVERDUE and DUE_SOON and null for calm states, on the principle that 'calm states don't shout.' The rail is decorative reinforcement, never the sole signal, since status is always also carried by chip and text. Verified already correct and explicitly preserved as-is in both DESIGN_SYSTEM_2026.md and the later Mobbin-informed blueprint.

nodes.label: Reminder Engine Reliability Risk
nodes.rationale: The entire scheduling strategy is a best-effort PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder(6h) with ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.KEEP, which is deferred by Doze, App Standby, and OEM process killers on Xiaomi/Huawei/Oppo/Vivo/Samsung/Realme -- most of the targeted South Asian market. There is no AlarmManager for date-critical items like insurance expiry, no exact-alarm permission, and zero battery-optimisation handling; KEEP also means a future schedule change never reaches existing installs. All four workers have zero tests. A maintenance app whose reminder silently fails is judged worse than no app at all, because the user believes they are covered and finds out only when something breaks.

nodes.label: Skeleton Shimmer vs Opacity-Pulse Conflict
nodes.rationale: DESIGN_SYSTEM_2026.md explicitly bans a translating shimmer sweep in favour of a 0.40->0.70 opacity pulse (1000ms, ease-in-out) because a translating gradient costs frames on every skeleton and reads as dated. Skeleton.kt's shipped shimmer() modifier is exactly the banned pattern -- an infiniteRepeatable animated linear-gradient sweep -- a real, present-tense drift between documented intent and shipped frame behaviour, though it correctly collapses to a static tint under reduced motion.

nodes.label: Status-Dependent Corner Radius as Shape Channel
nodes.norm_label: status-dependent corner radius as shape channel
nodes.rationale: DESIGN_SYSTEM_2026.md defends PremiumStatusStyle.cornerRadius() morphing 8dp (OVERDUE, sharp reads urgent) -> 16dp (DUE_SOON) -> 28dp (calm, soft reads safe) as one of four simultaneous status channels, never colour alone, and an already-accessibility-reviewed brand signature. mvp-plan.html's later 'Contradictions, resolved' table instead states this was 'Removed. Shape is set by component family' with status carried by icon/label/colour/rail/copy -- a genuine, unresolved tension between two governing documents from different sessions, explicitly flagged rather than silently decided in either direction by the Mobbin blueprint.

nodes.label: StatusCalculator Status Priority Algorithm
nodes.rationale: computeRaw takes the WORST of the date trigger and km trigger (OVERDUE < DUE_SOON < GOOD by severity); OVERDUE is evaluated before snooze and cannot itself be snoozed, so a critical reminder can never be silenced by an old snooze value. StatusCalculatorTest.kt is the authority; this document is explanation only.

nodes.label: Stitch Prior-Exploration Project 5215641449031779482
nodes.rationale: A prior in-house Google Stitch design exploration (46 entries, 4 markdown docs, 11 screenshots visually examined) contains screens that materially contradict AutoMinder's accountless, offline-first, no-telemetry product law: fabricated OBD-II-style gauges (tire PSI, fuel %, battery %, oil life) on nearly every dashboard variant, 'SYNCED'/'Cloud Sync Active' badges and a full Sync & Backup Center with named-device cloud restore, a complete email/SSO Login flow, and a Family Access flow with per-driver curfew/speed-limit fields implying GPS telemetry. All are explicitly rejected for v1.0 per CLAUDE.md's scope table, but because these are real, polished, high-fidelity mockups in a project titled after this app, a future session or non-engineering stakeholder could mistake them for approved direction.
